# Contributing

Thanks for helping. This is a small client library, so the process is light.

## Set up

```
uv sync --all-groups   # install deps + dev tools
uv run ruff check .    # lint
uv run mypy reportnet_api
uv run pytest          # no network needed: HTTP is mocked
```

All three must pass; CI runs the same commands on Python 3.11 to 3.14 and also builds the
wheel. The docs site is built with `uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict`.

## Generated files: do not hand-edit

- `reportnet_api/models/generated.py` is generated from `spec/api-docs.json`
  (`scripts/regen_models.sh`).
- `reportnet_api/resources/*.py` are generated by `scripts/generate_resources.py`
  (`scripts/regen_resources.sh`), except the hand-written `*_ext.py` modules.
- `docs/reference/*.md` is generated (`scripts/regen_docs.sh`) from the code, the spec
  and the notes in `scripts/docs_caveats.py`.

A manual fix to a generated file is silently lost on the next regeneration. Fix the
generator, the template or `docs_caveats.py` instead, regenerate, and commit the
regenerated output separately from hand-written changes.

## Tests and live behaviour

- Add a mocked test (`respx`) for every change in behaviour.
- Statements about what the live API does belong in `docs/live_testing_notes.md` with
  the date and how it was observed. Mark anything unverified as unverified.
- Never commit tokens, API keys, response captures or real dataflow/dataset ids, and
  keep personal data (emails, names) out of tests and docs: use `example.org`.
- Please do not run write or delete calls against a dataflow you do not own.

## Versions, releases and the changelog

Supported Python versions follow the upstream support window: when a Python version reaches
end of life it is dropped from `requires-python`, the classifiers and the CI matrix. Add a
line to `CHANGELOG.md` for every user-visible change; releases are described in
`docs/RELEASING.md`.

## Code of conduct

See [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Pull requests

Keep them small and focused, explain the reason for the change, and update the README
or reference where behaviour changes. By contributing you agree your work is released
under the project's MIT license.
